Event Planners in Parramatta

Parramatta plans big. Guest lists of three hundred are ordinary here, venues run from riverside function centres to the event halls at Sydney Olympic Park, and a planner who works this market quotes for that scale without blinking. Send one brief and hear back from planners who cover the area.

Get event planning quotesHow planning works
  • Sydney's geographic centreParramatta sits roughly halfway between the harbour and the Blue Mountains.
  • Built for scaleFunction rooms here are sized for three hundred guests, not eighty.
  • Light rail since 2024The line links the CBD, Westmead, Rosehill and Carlingford.

Three hundred guests is a normal Saturday here, not an ambitious one.

Parramatta grew around large families, large venues and a large calendar of cultural celebrations. Planners who work here build run sheets for multi day events as a matter of course.

The City of Parramatta is the geographic centre of Sydney and its second business district, which means an event here draws guests from the coast, the Hills and the west without asking any of them to cross the whole city. It also means scale. A large share of residents were born overseas, and the celebration calendar reflects that: three day programmes, ceremony and reception on separate days, and guest lists that start where other markets stop. The event planners in Parramatta who work this market quote for that as standard.

Venues sit in three bands. Riverside and civic function centres near the CBD, the purpose built precincts at Sydney Olympic Park and Rosehill, and a long tail of community halls and clubs through Northmead, Ermington and Winston Hills. Each carries a different set of rules about catering, alcohol and pack down times.

In and around Parramatta

What are you planning in Parramatta?

Most enquiries from this area fall into six shapes. The scale changes, the venue changes and the notice period changes, but the first conversation with a planner covers the same ground.

Start with

Weddings

Parramatta weddings are frequently multi day and frequently large. A planner here is used to a mehndi or engagement function on one day and a reception for three hundred on another, with separate venues, separate caterers and a family contact list that runs to two pages.

Find planners

Parties and milestones

First birthdays, sixtieths and anniversaries fill the community halls and club function rooms through Northmead, Dundas and Winston Hills. Those rooms usually come bare, so the planning work is hire, catering and a bump in window that is often only four hours long.

Find planners

Corporate events

The Parramatta CBD carries government departments, health services around Westmead and a growing professional services belt, which produces conferences, awards nights and staff functions on weekdays. Sydney Olympic Park handles anything that outgrows a hotel ballroom, including expos and full day programmes with breakouts.

Find planners

Engagement parties

An engagement party in this area is rarely small. Sixty to a hundred and fifty guests is common, both families are involved in the decisions, and the date often has to sit inside a religious calendar. A planner keeps the negotiation and the logistics apart.

Find planners

Proposals

The Parramatta River foreshore and the parklands around Rosehill and Olympic Park give a proposal somewhere green with a skyline behind it. Anything set up on council land needs a permit, and a planner handles that alongside the timing, the photographer and getting everyone into position unseen.

Find planners

Private celebrations

Naming ceremonies, religious milestones, graduations and family reunions run constantly here, often at short notice and often at home. Homes in Oatlands and Carlingford can take a marquee on the lawn; a planner sorts hire, catering flow and where two hundred cars go.

Planning support

How much help do you want in Parramatta?

Scale is the variable that decides how much help you need here. A hundred guests in a serviced function room is a coordination job. Three hundred across two days and two venues is a full planning job.

Full planning

A planner carries the whole build with you, from the first budget conversation to the last supplier leaving.

Usually engaged nine to fourteen months out.

  • Budget built and tracked
  • Venue and supplier shortlists
  • Contracts and payment schedule
  • Run sheet and floor plan
  • On the day, start to finish

You have made a start. A planner picks up the parts that have stalled and brings the rest into one plan.

Often engaged four to eight months out.

  • Picks up from where you are

  • Tidies the budget

  • Hands back a plan you can follow

On-the-day coordination

Your plan is built. A coordinator takes it over in the final weeks and runs the day so you can be in it.

Usually engaged four to eight weeks out.

  • Reads and stress-tests your plan
  • Confirms every supplier
  • Owns the run sheet
  • First point of contact on the day
  • Handles what goes sideways

Venue sourcing

Planners who know a market can shortlist against your date, your numbers and your budget rather than sending you back to the same search results.

Event coordination

Coordination is the execution layer: suppliers confirmed, a run sheet everyone has, and one person answering questions on the day.

Wedding coordination

A wedding coordinator takes a plan you have already built and runs the day itself, so nobody in the wedding party is directing traffic.

Choosing well

Finding the right planner in Parramatta

Ask questions that test whether a planner has actually worked at your size and in your community, rather than questions about taste. Four are worth putting in the first email.

No. 01

Ask about the biggest event they have run

Numbers change the job. Catering service style, bar queues, toilet ratios, seating plans and the time it takes to move three hundred people from a ceremony to a reception are all different at scale. A planner who works mostly at eighty guests may be excellent and still be learning on your event.

No. 02

Ask whether they have run your kind of ceremony

Cultural and religious events have fixed sequences, and the run sheet has to respect them. A planner who has run a South Asian, Middle Eastern or Pacific Island wedding before will not need the order of the day explained, and will already know which suppliers understand it.

No. 03

Check who owns the external caterer relationship

Community halls and club rooms in this area commonly allow an outside caterer, and some require one. Confirm whether the planner books and manages that caterer or whether you do, because kitchen access, service staff numbers and the pack down clean are the parts that fall through the gap between the two.

No. 04

Get the travel and site visit terms in writing

Planners quote a service area, and Parramatta sits inside most Sydney planners' radius. What varies is site visits. If your ceremony is in Parramatta and your reception is at Olympic Park or Rosehill, that is two site visits plus a rehearsal, and some planners charge for each one past the first.

A planner who has never run three hundred guests will learn the hard parts on your day.

On the ground

What three hundred guests does to a Parramatta run sheet

Three things shape event logistics in this council area: the size of the average guest list, the construction still under way across the CBD, and the river that runs through the middle of it.

Getting three hundred people in and out

Scale breaks the parts of a plan nobody thinks about. Three hundred guests need three hundred car spaces unless you organise otherwise, and the Parramatta CBD car parks fill on Saturdays with people who are not at your event. Planners here routinely build a transport plan: a coach from the ceremony to the reception, a marshalled drop off point, and instructions that go out with the invitation, not on the day. The other pressure point is service. A room that seats three hundred needs a caterer who can serve three hundred within forty minutes, and that is a staffing question you settle at booking, not at the tasting.

Construction is a real variable

Parramatta Light Rail opened in 2024 and Sydney Metro West is still being built underneath the CBD, so the street network changes from one year to the next. That matters for two things: where a coach can legally stop, and how long a twenty minute transfer actually takes on a Saturday afternoon. Ask your venue for its current drop off arrangement rather than trusting a map, and build fifteen minutes of slack into any transfer that crosses Church Street or Macquarie Street. Guests arriving by train now have a light rail leg as well, which is an improvement once they know it exists.

The river, and the two big precincts

The Parramatta River is the one piece of geography that gives this area an outlook, and it is also a transport option: the ferry runs downstream to Circular Quay, which is worth knowing if part of your guest list is coming from the harbour side of the city. Two precincts sit inside the council area and behave differently from an ordinary venue.

  • Sydney Olympic Park: purpose built, very large, with its own parking, transport and event rules.
  • Rosehill: a racing precinct, so check the race calendar before you set a date.
  • The foreshore parks: council land, which means a permit for anything you set up.

Questions

Planning an event in Parramatta

How much does an event planner cost in Parramatta?

There is no Parramatta rate, because planners price the scope rather than the postcode. Airtasker (updated February 2025) puts event planning across Australia at $1,000 to $20,000 with a median near $8,000, and describes hourly and percentage of budget models as common alternatives. A three hundred guest event over two days sits well above a single afternoon function on any of those models, so quote the real guest count from the start.

Do Parramatta planners handle multi day cultural weddings?

Many do, and it is worth asking directly rather than assuming. A three day programme is not one event repeated: each day has its own venue, its own supplier list, its own timing rules and often its own guest list. Ask a planner which specific ceremonies they have run, how they handled the handover between days, and whether they will be on site for all of them or only the reception.

Can I hold an event at Sydney Olympic Park through a planner?

Yes, and a planner is genuinely useful there because the precinct runs to its own rules. Sydney Olympic Park sits inside the City of Parramatta and operates as a managed event precinct, with its own access, parking, loading and scheduling arrangements, and several major events on at once on a busy weekend. A planner who has worked there will know the bump in windows and build your run sheet backwards from them.

How far ahead should I book for a Parramatta wedding?

Twelve to eighteen months if you want a large room on a Saturday between March and May or in October and November. Parramatta has a limited number of venues that genuinely seat three hundred, and they are booked by the same peak season demand as the rest of Sydney plus the cultural calendar. If your date has to avoid Ramadan, Lent or a specific festival, start earlier again, because the workable weekends narrow quickly.

Will a Sydney CBD planner travel to Parramatta?

Almost always, since Parramatta sits inside the standard Sydney service radius for most planners. The cost that does move is site visits. A CBD based planner driving to Westmead or Rosehill for a walkthrough, a tasting and a rehearsal is making three separate trips, and some quote a fee past the first. Ask how many visits are included and what happens if your ceremony and reception are in different suburbs.

Does a planner book the caterer and the other suppliers?

Yes, that is a core part of the job. A planner shortlists suppliers, negotiates the quotes, holds the contracts in one place and manages the schedule on the day, which for a Parramatta event usually means a caterer, a hire company, florals, entertainment and a photographer. You still choose and you still pay them, and a planner should tell you plainly whether they take a commission from anyone they recommend.
